read.thesis: Gas turbine slot reservations and orders rose to 116 GW with a 125 GW year-end target, Electrification book-to-bill near 1.7, and Power segment margin up 240 bps; supply-side discipline shows in gas output steps (20 GW in Q3 2026, 24 GW in 2028, 30 GW in 2030 under action).

utilisation.quote: we remain on track to deliver 20 GW of annual gas turbine output in the third quarter of 2026, with 24 GW in 2028, and we are implementing actions to produce 30 GW in 2030

capex.quote: Invested $0.4 billion in capital expenditures, including to increase production in Power and Electrification, as part of its commitment to invest $6 in capex from 2025 through 2028

triggers.label: Gas slot reservations+orders 100→116 GW
triggers.quote: Gas Power equipment backlog and slot reservation agreements grew from 100 to 116 GW; now anticipate reaching at least 125 GW by year-end 2026

triggers.label: Power EBITDA margin +240 bps
triggers.quote: Segment EBITDA margin grew +240 basis points, +320 basis points organically

triggers.label: FCF guidance raised to $11.5-12.5B
triggers.quote: free cash flow* of $11.5-$12.5 billion, up from $6.5-$7.5 billion

triggers.label: Wind orders down 39% organically
triggers.quote: $1.2 billion decreased (40)% organically driven by lower Onshore Wind equipment orders

guidance.quote: now expects revenue of $45.5-$46.5 billion, up from $44.5-$45.5 billion
free cash flow* of $11.5-$12.5 billion, up from $6.5-$7.5 billion
Power: 18%-20% organic revenue* growth, up from 16%-18%
Revenue of $14.5-$15.0 billion, inclusive of approximately $3.1 billion from Prolec GE

guidance.metric: Gas equipment under contract by YE2026
guidance.quote: now anticipate reaching at least 125 GW by year-end 2026
we remain on track to deliver 20 GW of annual gas turbine output in the third quarter of 2026

red_flags.label: FCF boosted by working capital
red_flags.quote: Free cash flow* of $5.1 increased $4.9, primarily due to higher positive benefits from working capital and stronger adjusted EBITDA*

red_flags.label: Wind equipment orders collapse
red_flags.quote: $1.2 billion decreased (40)% organically driven by lower Onshore Wind equipment orders
